subject: SLA evidence & throughput verification plan for Dedicated commit
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmeai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA evidence & throughput verification plan for Dedicated commit

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a short proposal for how Redwood will evidence throughput guarantees for the Dedicated GPU pool tied to Acme's 12‑month reserved commit. Key items below so we can align quickly: 

- Proposed guarantee: baseline of 120k tokens/sec aggregate across the reserved pool (measured as produced tokens/sec at the model output) with a P95 SLA target for per-request latency (see latency bullets).
- Measurement window: we propose a rolling 60‑minute window for tokens/sec assessment; SLA violations are calculated on P95 over that window (see test cases).
- Latency targets: P95 end-to-end (request enter -> first token emitted) less than 250ms for short completions (<=32 tokens); for longer completions we will publish expected median per-token latency curves.
- Warm/cold behavior: verification runs will include a 10‑minute warmup for KV cache and model loading; steady-state measurement begins after warmup.
- Credits / remediation: if Redwood misses the guaranteed throughput for two consecutive hourly windows, we propose a credit calculated as (missed_percent * committed_monthly_fee). Details in attachments.
- Discount/packaging note: proposed committed discount tiers attached (Dedicated_Commit_Tiers.xlsx). The 12‑month commit you referenced qualifies for our 18% committed discount at the 4‑GPU pool level, with an additional negotiation space for bumped SLOs.

Attachments: SLA_Test_Case_Definitions.pdf (test vectors + harness), Dedicated_Commit_Tiers.xlsx (pricing tiers).

Action: please confirm the measurement definitions that matter to Acme (tokens/sec produced vs tokens/sec requested, acceptable warmup, and acceptable credit calculation) and whether you need a quarterly independent validation clause. If you agree, we'll schedule an initial validation run and produce the raw CSVs and traces for your team.

Cheers,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Strategic Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmeai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@acmeai.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA evidence & throughput verification plan for Dedicated commit

Thanks Jordan — this is a helpful start. A few clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

1) Tokens/sec definition: are you measuring tokens/sec at the generation output (i.e., tokens/sec produced by the model), or based on incoming request tokens (prompt + expected output)? For our billing/contracting we prefer produced tokens/sec.

2) Requests/sec vs tokens/sec: our workload has a mix of short queries (<=16 tokens) and longer summarizations (~512 tokens). How will you map the guarantee so short bursts of small requests don't skew the aggregate? Is there a per-request QoS floor?

3) Warmup: 10 minutes seems short if you're relying on KV cache for long-session chat workloads. Can you detail the warm/cold treatment and whether the SLA excludes initial deployment/scale events?

4) Validation harness: we need the test harness to be runnable by our infra team (k8s job or container). Will Redwood provide the harness and test vectors as Docker images? We also require access to the raw logs (CSV) and the exact test runner configuration used for the official validation runs.

5) Credits: need an example calculation and explanation of how credits are invoked (auto or require claim). Also want an upper cap on credits to avoid perverse incentives.

If you can answer these in writing I can share with Legal and Procurement. We're generally comfortable with a committed discount if the verification method is transparent and repeatable.

Best,
Maya Patel
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme AI
maya.patel@acmeai.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA evidence & throughput verification plan for Dedicated commit (technical clarifications)

Jordan / Grace —

Quick technical notes to answer Maya's outstanding items; feel free to paste these back to Acme with our standard legal wording.

1) Measurement semantics (recommendation): we propose produced tokens/sec at the output as the primary metric (this matches customer expectations and avoids inflation by prompt-only requests). For each second we count tokens emitted by the model process and compute a sliding 60‑minute aggregate. The SLA evaluates the minimum of the observed aggregate across all GPUs in the reserved pool vs the guaranteed aggregate.

2) Handling mixed length workloads: we'll run workload-weighted test vectors reflecting a 65/35 split short/long (customer-defined mix). For contract purposes we offer two options: (a) single aggregate tokens/sec guarantee using the customer-specified mix, or (b) partitioned guarantees — e.g., X tokens/sec for short-requests bucket and Y tokens/sec for long-requests bucket. Partitioning gives clearer isolation for your short query SLAs.

3) Warm/cold policy: verification runs will include a defined 10‑minute warmup for cache population. We will exclude automated scale/instance rollout windows (platform-initiated machine restarts) from credit calculations, but not exclude customer traffic spikes. We can add a 'deployment window' exclusion clause (e.g., up to four scheduled maintenance events per quarter).

4) Test harness delivery: Redwood will deliver a containerized test harness (Docker image) with: test runner, vector corpus (from SLA_Test_Case_Definitions.pdf), an orchestration script (k8s job manifest example), and a results exporter to CSV and OpenTelemetry traces. We'll provide SHA256 for images and a runbook describing parameters (concurrency, request pacing, seed randomization). The official run will be executed by Redwood in collaboration with Acme infra; raw logs and CSVs will be shared via a secure S3 link (or SFTP) within 24 hours of completion.

5) Credits & calculation example: credit = missed_percent_of_guarantee * monthly_commit_fee, capped at 20% of monthly fee per calendar month. Triggering: automatic bookkeeping by Redwood with notification + 10 business day dispute window. If Acme disputes results we provide raw harness logs and test configuration for review; final remediation follows our dispute SLA.

6) Latency specifics: P95 first-token latency target for <=32 token completions is 250ms. We'll publish per-token delta curves for longer sequences; those are informative but not credit-bearing unless explicitly added to the contract.

I'll draft a short appendix with concrete CSV field names and example lines for the official report.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SLA evidence & throughput verification plan for Dedicated commit

Jordan —

Thanks to you and Aditya for the detailed responses. Acme is prepared to move forward with the 12‑month committed package subject to the following adjustments we discussed internally: 

- Confirmation that Redwood will measure produced tokens/sec (as defined).
- Add a quarterly verification run (jointly scheduled) with results delivered within 24 hours of completion.
- Include a 10% "burst allowance" for one‑minute spikes per day (this protects short bursty traffic patterns).
- Credits calculation as proposed, but cap set to 15% of monthly fee (we're asking for a slightly lower cap).

We've signed the non‑binding MOU and attached the PDF (MOU_AcmeAI_signed.pdf). Legal will send DocuSign for the final SOW/commit next week. Please provide the Docker image tag for the test harness and a proposed calendar for the initial validation run.
